_comment: Copy to approved-mints.json. Nothing runs live until dryRun is explicitly set to false for a target. This file is your Risk-Committee-equivalent sign-off record — keep it under version control so changes are reviewable. Entries with a _verification block were drafted by the mint-intelligence agent from live research and still need a human to close out anything under _verification.unresolvedFields before they're trustworthy, let alone before dryRun ever goes false.

gogh-punks-robinhood._comment: Researched by mint-intelligence on 2026-08-13, updated after user-supplied Blockscout link confirmed this is a SeaDrop mint, updated again after user supplied the real feeRecipient address read from the SeaDrop contract. Updated again 2026-08-14 after a live getPublicDrop() read via the diagnostic bridge corrected two wrong fields: valueEth was 10x too high, and the trigger timestamp was exactly one day early. contractAddress below is the SHARED SeaDrop router contract, NOT the Gogh Punks NFT contract — the NFT contract address is passed as mintArgs[0] instead.
gogh-punks-robinhood.contractAddressLabel: OpenSea SeaDrop router (shared across many collections, not Gogh-Punks-specific)
gogh-punks-robinhood.nftContractLabel: GoghPunksOnchain — the actual collection, confirmed verified on Blockscout as ERC721SeaDrop

trigger._comment: 2026-08-15 23:15:00 UTC — read live from the SeaDrop contract's getPublicDrop(nftContract).startTime via the diagnostic bridge on 2026-08-14. This is one full day later than the drop-calendar's originally stated time; trust this over the calendar.

mintMechanicsSources: https://nftcalendar.io/event/gogh-punks-public-mi/ (initial lead, since superseded on timing/price — see below)

Live on-chain read via getPublicDrop(nftContract) through the diagnostic bridge, 2026-08-14 — this is now the authoritative source for startTime, endTime, mintPrice, maxTotalMintableByWallet, feeBps, restrictFeeRecipients
nftContractAddressSources: https://robinhoodchain.blockscout.com/api/v2/smart-contracts/0xe0f92b3b0e6ded3654177fe3809cd300e5ffadf6 — verified contract, name GoghPunksOnchain, implements ERC721SeaDrop, supply constants (10000/9500/500) match the drop-calendar figures independently
mintFunctionSources: https://robinhoodchain.blockscout.com/api/v2/smart-contracts/0x00005EA00Ac477B1030CE78506496e8C2dE24bf5 — mintPublic(address nftContract, address feeRecipient, address minterIfNotPayer, uint256 quantity), confirmed payable
feeRecipientSources: User-supplied, read directly from the SeaDrop contract's getAllowedFeeRecipients(nftContract) via Blockscout's Read Contract tab on 0x00005EA00Ac477B1030CE78506496e8C2dE24bf5.
Independently re-confirmed live via getFeeRecipientIsAllowed(nftContract, feeRecipient) through the diagnostic bridge, 2026-08-14 — returned true.
valueEthSources: Live on-chain read via getPublicDrop(nftContract).mintPrice through the diagnostic bridge, 2026-08-14 — 300000000000000 wei = 0.0003 ETH. Corrects the drop-calendar's stated 0.003 ETH, which was 10x too high.
triggerSources: Live on-chain read via getPublicDrop(nftContract).startTime through the diagnostic bridge, 2026-08-14 — 1786835700 (2026-08-15T23:15:00Z). Corrects the drop-calendar's stated time, which was exactly one day early.
unresolvedFields: mintArgs[2] (minterIfNotPayer = address(0)) — set from general SeaDrop-protocol knowledge (address(0) commonly means 'mint to the payer'), not verified against SeaDrop's own source/docs. getPublicDrop doesn't expose this — no on-chain read can close it out. Confirm against the natspec comment on mintPublic in https://github.com/ProjectOpenSea/seadrop before ever going live; not blocking for a dry run.
_verification.notes: The 2026-08-14 dry-run failure ('missing revert data') traced to two real config errors, both now corrected from a live getPublicDrop() read: valueEth was 10x too high (0.003 vs actual 0.0003), and the trigger timestamp was exactly one day early (drop-calendar said Aug 14 23:15 UTC; the contract's actual startTime is Aug 15 23:15 UTC). trigger.mode was also found set to "immediate" rather than "timestamp", which is why the simulation attempted the mint right away instead of waiting — reset to "timestamp" with the corrected value. Only mintArgs[2]'s convention remains an unverified guess, and it's not something any on-chain read can resolve — everything else is now confirmed live, not just cross-sourced.
